catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class binds a single persistent ROS geometry_msgs/Twist publication whose upstream callback has no acknowledgement, no duration and no measured distance or heading. cap.motion.mobile_base.v1 requires a bounded duration and distance/heading output, which the /cmd_vel callback does not provide; the receipt can only report transmission. The receipt also reports the three Twist components handed to rosbridge.
No catalogue class observes nav_msgs/Odometry. The motion classes command motion and do not carry a pose and body-twist subscription output.
No catalogue class observes a generic sensor_msgs/JointState stream. cap.motion.joint_position.v1 commands joint positions and does not describe a read-only joint observation.
No catalogue class observes a simulated ROS clock. The world classes advance, reset, seed or render a simulator but do not carry a rosgraph_msgs/Clock subscription output.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked every endpoint and type (/cmd_vel through the launch remap of the controller's relative cmd_vel/smooth subscription, spot.gazebo.launch.py:111-113 and quadruped_controller.cpp:69-70, and the three bridged observations, spot_bridge.yaml:3-16), all 15 facts and the stop: the clone serves no ROS service or action and bridges none, the /cmd_vel callback only stores the last Twist (116-121) and a wall timer keeps applying it (94-113), so no acknowledged stop exists and the stock e-stop fails G6.ESTOP_FAILED and G8 SAFE-028 with the latch held; the package drives an Ignition Gazebo simulation with no hardware path, so the blocker is HELPER_MISSING, not the author's NO_HARDWARE_FREE_PATH. Defects fixed: the three velocity limits cited gait.yaml lines that show only the positive caps, so collect.py --strict printed three UNSOURCED_LIMIT_GATE_WARNINGs (the negative bounds are only the negation in leg_controller.h:96-98, and the controller clamps instead of refusing); the clock schema used the ROS 1 names secs/nsecs, so a reviewer probe showed every real ROS 2 Clock refused as MHS.CAPABILITY.OUTPUT_INVALID; the twist vectors carried unit 1; and a fact claimed 'on every timer tick' outside its range. Reviewer changed driver.py (Limit.operator_required for the three velocities, sec/nanosec clock schema, m/s and rad/s twist units, the control-loop fact narrowed, two timer facts and three fidelity gaps added), fake.py (ROS 2 clock fields), test_driver.py (served cases use the example overlay, a new case refuses a velocity without it, the clock case expects sec/nanosec), facts.md and a new site-limits.example.json (the gait.yaml caps as an example), and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json. The gate now fails only G6.ESTOP_FAILED and G8 SAFE-028, collect.py --strict shows no warning, and the seven package cases pass; the author's notes on NO_HARDWARE_FREE_PATH and on the three sourced gait.yaml limits are superseded. For the human reviewer: Simulation only (CHAMP controller on Ignition Gazebo Fortress); no hardware path in the clone. No ROS stop exists: the world's WorldControl play/pause is a GUI plugin, not a ROS service, and spot_bridge.yaml bridges no service. The CHAMP controller runs on a wall timer and keeps applying the last /cmd_vel and publishing joint trajectories, also while Gazebo is paused; any later /cmd_vel from any client changes it, and the README's navigation steps launch spot_navigation (not in the clone), whose stack publishes /cmd_vel. With the bridged observation topics silent every command waits the 2 s read timeout (reviewer probe). Unblocking needs an acknowledged simulator pause or stop that a clone line names, or an SDK route for topic-only simulators.
